_about: Field terms for F320, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

auc.definition: the probability that a classifier gives a randomly chosen positive case a higher score than a randomly chosen negative case; 0.5 is chance and 1 is perfect separation
auc.excludes: accuracy at one threshold, and any statement about how well the scores are calibrated as probabilities

overlapping-windows.definition: fixed-length stretches cut from a recording at a step shorter than their length, so that neighbouring windows share samples; here 60 s windows every 15 s share 75 percent of their samples
overlapping-windows.excludes: windows cut end to end with no shared samples

random-split.field: machine learning evaluation; called record-wise cross-validation in the clinical literature
random-split.definition: assigning windows to training and test sets at random, so that windows from the same person and the same recording block fall on both sides
random-split.excludes: any split that keeps all of one person's data on one side

loso.field: machine learning evaluation; called subject-wise cross-validation
loso.definition: training on all people but one and scoring on the one left out, repeated so that each person is held out once
loso.excludes: a test on people from another study, lab or protocol

within-person-auc.definition: the AUC computed on one held-out person's windows alone, then averaged over people; it asks whether the classifier ranks that person's stress windows above their other windows
within-person-auc.excludes: the global AUC, which pools all held-out windows and also rewards separating people from each other

random-forest.definition: a classifier that averages many decision trees, each grown on a resampled copy of the training data with a random subset of features tried at each split; here 100 trees with at least 3 windows per leaf
random-forest.excludes: any model tuned on the test person

logistic-regression.definition: a classifier that models the log odds of the positive class as a weighted sum of the features; here on standardised features with an L2 (ridge) penalty at strength C = 1
logistic-regression.excludes: interactions between features, which it does not model unless they are added by hand

tsst.definition: a laboratory stressor in which a person prepares and gives a short public talk and then does mental arithmetic aloud in front of an evaluating panel
tsst.excludes: daily stress, chronic stress and trauma

stai.definition: a short form of the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory in which a person rates six statements about how they feel at that moment; positive items are reverse scored so that a higher total means more anxiety
stai.excludes: a clinical diagnosis, and anxiety as a lasting trait

eda.definition: the electrical conductance of the skin, which rises with sweat gland activity under sympathetic nervous control
eda.excludes: a direct reading of emotion; temperature and movement also change it

planted-shift.definition: a fixed amount added to one feature in every stress window of every person in planted data, in the same direction for all, so that a classifier tested on a new person has something real to find
planted-shift.excludes: the per-person, per-block offsets, which point in a random direction and carry nothing from one person to the next

ceiling-auc.definition: the AUC a perfect reader of the one shifted feature could reach when the stress and non-stress values of that feature are normal with a variance of 1.09 each (a block offset of variance 1 plus window noise of variance 0.09)
ceiling-auc.excludes: the effect of the 19 features that carry no shift, and of the small number of people

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false discoveries stays at or below a chosen level q
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: control of the chance of even one false discovery, which is a stricter rule

spearman-rho.definition: the correlation between the ranks of two quantities; it runs from -1 to 1 and measures how well one quantity's order follows the other's, whatever the shape of the relation
spearman-rho.excludes: the size of the change, and any causal direction

cluster-bootstrap.definition: redrawing people with replacement, 2,000 times, and recomputing the mean of the per-person scores each time; the middle 95 percent of those means is the interval
cluster-bootstrap.excludes: redrawing single windows, which would treat one person's many windows as many independent people
